title: PackError
description:
A pack's failure report. The single `error` key keeps this document
distinguishable from any other JSON a pack may print.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable identifier for this kind of failure, such as
`baseline_failed`. Codes are `lower_snake_case` and outlive any wording
change to `message`.

message.description:
Human-readable explanation of the failure. For display only: consumers
branch on `stage` and `code`, never on this text.

stage.description: The step of the pack's work that failed.

Stage.description:
The steps of a pack run, in the order a pack performs them, plus the steps of
the calls that are not a run. A `stage` tells the core how far the pack got,
which distinguishes a project problem such as a failing baseline from an
adapter problem such as a failed plan.

Any string is valid here. A consumer reads a value this contract version does not define as `unknown` rather than refusing the document that carries it, so a validator must not refuse it either. The values this version does define:
- `preflight` — Checking the environment before any work starts.
- `spans` — Reading a source file's functions, before any manifest exists.
- `probe` — Running one input against both versions of a function.
- `validate` — Language-level validation of the manifest.
- `baseline` — The unmutated reference run.
- `plan` — Turning the manifest into work items for the execution backend.
- `execute` — Applying mutants and running the suite.
- `collect` — Reading results back out of the backend's state.
- `unknown` — A step this consumer does not know, reported by a newer pack. The failure is still a failure and still carries a code and a message; only where it happened is beyond what this consumer can name.
